text: Among the lonely green hills of Wessex there once stood a solitary cottage called Higher Crowstairs, far from any village and open to every wind. <break time="0.8s" /> On the night of March 28, in a year long ago, a fierce storm swept over the hills, and the rain struck the walls like flying arrows. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside, however, all was warm and bright, for Shepherd Fennel and his wife were holding a party to celebrate the christening of their second daughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Nineteen people, most of them shepherds and farm workers with their wives, were dancing to the music of a fiddle played by a boy of twelve. <break time="0.8s" /> Missus Fennel, a careful housekeeper, secretly worried that the long dancing would make her guests hungry and thirsty enough to empty her cupboards. <break time="0.8s" /> At about the same time, a lonely figure was climbing the hill through the rain, having come on foot from the direction of the distant town of Casterbridge. <break time="0.8s" /> Tall and thin, with his clothes soaked by the storm, he stopped near the door and drank thirstily from a stone basin full of rainwater. <break time="0.8s" /> He listened for a while to the music and laughter inside, as though he could not decide whether to knock or to walk on into the dark.
